title: Extracellular Exosomes Link Hypertension and Alzheimer’s Disease
projectDescription: Untreated hypertension is a risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer’s disease (AD); however, this association is not well understood. The aim of this study was to reveal protein signatures that bridge the pathophysiological changes in hypertension to AD. Using untargeted proteomics, we analyzed frontal cortex brain samples from aged (30- and 40-week-old) spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs, n = 12), and age-matched normotensive Wistar Kyoto (WKY, n = 8) controls, and human AD patients (Braak stages 4-6) (n = 30), cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) (n = 5), non-demented controls (Braak stages 0-3) (n = 37). Following differential expression analyses in each species, we identified 24 proteins in SHRs and AD, whose trajectory pattern over the progression of hypertension, aligned with those observed during AD Braak stage progression, compared to respective controls. The proteins were significantly associated with extracellular exosomes. Immunostaining and spatial proteomics support vesicle accumulation and dysregulated exosome protein signatures in the cerebrovasculature of both SHR and AD brains. Our findings demonstrate cross-species translatability between AD and the SHR and provide novel mechanistic insights into a shared dysregulation of cerebral artery-associated exosomes.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) membrane slides (Applied BiosystemsTM, LCM0522) were coated with Vectabond (Vector Laboratories, Cat. No. SP-1800-7) following the manufacturer’s instructions. FFPE tissue sections were mounted onto pre-treated slides and dried at RT. Slides were deparaffinized, rehydrated and subjected to antigen retrieval as described in the Histology section. Sections were stained with anti-alpha smooth muscle actin antibody [1A4] (ab7817, produced in Mouse, 1:400, Abcam) and counterstained with anti-mouse HRP-conjugated EnVision+ detection reagent (DAKO, Cat. No. K4001) for 30 minutes at RT. Signal development was performed using the 3,3′-diaminobenzidine (DAB) Bright system (ImmunoLogic, Cat. No. VWEKBS04-500) for 8 minutes. Slides were then rinsed in distilled water, stained with Mayer’s hematoxylin for 30 seconds, wash under running tap water for 7 min and rinsed in deionized water for 3 min. The membrane was punctured by creating small holes and dried for 45 min at 60 °C followed by storage at RT until laser dissection.  Regions of interest (artery, capillary or adjacent parenchyma) were cut using the LMD7 (Leica) laser microdissection system with the following settings: Power = 30, Aperture = 15, Speed = 20, Specimen balance = 15, Head current = 100%, Puls frequency = 120. The microscope was operated with the LMD v8.2 software, with ThreeSlides sample holder and the standard PCR tube collector (4 tubes). A total tissue area of approximately 200.000 µm2 were collected per region into a 0.2 ml thin walled and flat capped PCR tube (Axygen, PCR-02-C). The dissected elements were confirmed by visual inspection under microscope. Tubes were centrifuged at 5000 g for 10 min, then 25 ul of digestion buffer was added to the cap and tubes were centrifuged again. Tubes were heated for 1 hour at 95 °C in a heat block, cooled to RT and centrifuged for 30 sec at 5000 g. Samples were reduced and alkylated by adding 0.5 ul TCEP (0.5 M, Sigma) and 2.5 ul CAA (0.5 M, Sigma) followed by 20 min incubation at 37 °C. Subsequently, 20 ng of Trypsin/LysC mix (Promega, cat no. V5072) was added and proteins were digested overnight at 37 °C. Samples were desalted as described in the Sample preparation for proteomics section and subsequently reconstituted in 7 ul reconstitution buffer. Peptide mixtures were analyzed on Bruker timsTOF mass spectrometer using positive ion mode, with a Captivespray ion source on-line connected to a Dionex Ultimate 3000RSnano chromatography system (Thermo Fisher).
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw DIA files were analyzed with DIA-NN software (v.1.9).An in silico DIA-NN predicted spectral library was generated using UniProt FASTA databases for Homo sapiens (UP000005640_9606).Protein quantities obtained from DIA-NN were analyzed using Perseus (v1.6.14.0). A Two-sided Student’s t-test was conducted. Enrichment analysis of differentially expressed proteins identified was performed with the STRING app (v2.0.1) in Cytoscape (v3.9.1).
